set.title: Georgia Entry Requirements 2026: Visa & Insurance Checklist
set.metaTitle: Georgia Entry Requirements 2026: Visa & Insurance Checklist
set.metaDescription: Check Georgia entry requirements for 2026: visa-free eligibility, GCC resident rules, mandatory 30,000 GEL insurance and documents to prepare before you fly.
set.excerpt: Check your tourist-entry route, GCC residence-permit conditions, mandatory insurance and border documents, with links to official Georgian sources.

children.text: Georgia entry requirements in 2026 depend on your passport, any qualifying foreign visa or residence permit, and the purpose of your visit. Tourists covered by the insurance rules must also carry health and accident insurance with at least 30,000 GEL of cover for the full stay. Use the checklist below to identify your entry route and prepare the documents before travelling to Georgia, the country in the Caucasus.
Last checked: 27 October 2026. This guide covers tourist trips; confirm your individual eligibility with Georgia's consular authorities before booking if your documents or status are unclear.
Georgia entry requirements: your pre-flight checklist
Prepare a travel folder for each person, including children:
A valid passport or another travel document accepted for your specific entry route.
A Georgian visa, if required, or the documents proving your visa-free eligibility.
Health and accident insurance that meets the tourist-entry requirements.
Accommodation details, your trip plan and return or onward arrangements.
Evidence that you can fund the visit, ready to show if requested.

Keep names, passport details and travel dates consistent across bookings and documents. Save copies offline as well as keeping the originals available. A confirmation stored only in an email account is less useful when you cannot get online at check-in.
Start with the
official Georgian consular portal
, entering your citizenship, passport type, intended stay and any qualifying foreign visa or residence permit. The country you fly from alone does not determine whether you need a visa.
Do you need a visa for Georgia?
Visa-free entry based on citizenship

Georgia allows citizens of many listed countries to visit without obtaining a visa in advance. The one-year category includes citizens of the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and the six GCC states: Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman.
The wording for that category is one full year, not “365 days per calendar year.” Do not treat January as a reset or assume that every visa-exempt nationality has the same permitted stay. The
official tourism visa information
provides an overview; use the consular check for your own circumstances.

Visa-free eligibility does not remove the need for supporting documents or determine the final border decision. It also should not be used as a substitute for checking requirements for employment, study or residence. Those purposes fall outside this tourist guide.
Entry using a foreign visa or residence permit

Some travellers who would otherwise need a Georgian visa can qualify through a visa or residence permit issued by a listed country. This is a separate route, generally allowing 90 days in any 180-day period, subject to the applicable conditions.

Check the document itself, its issuer, validity and any nationality-specific restriction. Living in another country is not enough without the qualifying status and evidence. A family member's eligibility also does not automatically establish yours.

If your document is being renewed, expires close to the trip or exists only as a temporary confirmation, ask the Georgian consulate which evidence it will accept before committing to travel. Describe the actual document rather than relying on a general question such as “Can residents visit?”
Georgia visa rules for GCC residents

GCC citizens and foreign residents of GCC countries should check different entry routes. A Saudi passport holder and an Indian or Pakistani passport holder living in Saudi Arabia do not automatically have the same conditions.
The
Georgian Embassy's UAE guidance
distinguishes UAE citizens' one-year visa-free stay from eligible UAE residents' 90 days in any 180 days. It says the UAE residence document must be valid on entry and departure.

A stricter condition applies to nationals of 17 specified countries using the relevant Gulf visa or residence-permit route: the qualifying document must have at least one year of remaining validity at entry, with a multiple-entry condition where a visa is used. This is not a blanket one-year requirement for every GCC resident.

The affected nationalities include Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Ghana, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, Sudan, Syria, Tanzania, Uganda and Yemen. Georgia's
Interior Ministry explanation of the Gulf-document rule
identifies this restricted group.

If you fall within it and your document has less than a year remaining, contact the Georgian consulate about the appropriate visa route. Do not infer approval from another traveller's experience. For itinerary planning after checking eligibility, see our
Georgia family guide for Gulf travellers
Georgia visa for Indian passport holders

An ordinary Indian passport does not by itself place the traveller in the general one-year visa-free category. A qualifying foreign visa or residence permit can change the entry route; otherwise, check whether you meet the current e-Visa conditions or need a consular application.

Use the official portal with both your passport nationality and your actual supporting documents. Avoid treating “Indian traveller from Dubai” as a complete eligibility description: the residence status and the documents carried matter.

For a family travelling together, make a separate check for each person. A spouse, child or other relative may hold a different passport or residence document. Resolve those differences before making bookings that cannot be changed.
Applying for a Georgian e-Visa
The
official e-Visa FAQ

says a decision takes at least five working days. Apply with a buffer; “at least” is not a guaranteed delivery date. Follow the portal's current nationality and document checks rather than assuming everyone can use the same application route.

For an e-Visa application, the FAQ specifies a passport issued within the previous ten years, at least two blank pages and validity extending at least three months beyond the requested visa's validity period. These are the published e-Visa passport conditions; do not turn them into a universal passport rule for every visa-free visitor.

Each traveller who needs an e-Visa must apply separately, including children. Check the issued document against the passport before departure and carry the required copy. If there is a mismatch, resolve it through the official process before travel.
Is travel insurance mandatory for Georgia in 2026?
Yes, for incoming tourists covered by Government Decree No. 602, effective from 1 January 2026. The
Georgian Embassy's insurance notice
sets out the main requirements:
Health and accident insurance, with an insured amount of at least 30,000 GEL.
Coverage throughout the visit, including arrival and departure dates.
A policy available in Georgian or English, on paper or electronically.
A policy from a Georgian or foreign insurance company.

The 30,000 GEL figure is the minimum insured amount, not the premium you pay. Compare the policy wording as well as the headline limit: benefit restrictions, deductibles and excluded activities affect what protection you actually have.
What should the policy document show?
Under
Decree No. 602
, the policy records the contracting parties, covered territory, insured subject, start and end times, insured risks, limits and premium/payment information.

Ask the insurer for a document that clearly identifies Georgia as covered territory and your full travel period. If using an existing annual or employer policy, obtain confirmation of the relevant cover instead of assuming a membership card is sufficient.

For family cover, check that every travelling person is identified and covered. If the policy groups several travellers under one contract, ask the insurer to explain the limits applying to each insured person. Carry a readable copy that makes the family members easy to identify.
Exemptions and special circumstances

The decree lists specific exceptions, including diplomatic and special visa or passport categories, accredited diplomatic personnel and qualifying family members, entry covered by relevant international agreements, and drivers involved in international road freight or passenger transport.

It applies to incoming tourists; this guide does not classify every residence, work or other non-tourist situation. If you rely on an exemption, obtain guidance for your exact status rather than assuming it from property ownership or a long previous stay.
Buying cover before departure
Arrange insurance before travelling and check when protection starts. Do not plan around buying a policy from a border officer or assume there will be a suitable product available when you arrive.
If you use
VisitorsCoverage to compare travel insurance
, check the chosen policy's wording against Georgia's requirements directly with the insurer. A comparison listing or purchase confirmation is not a guarantee that every product meets your needs.
This post contains an affiliate link. If you buy through it, it does not cost you anything extra and helps support this site.
Documents to keep ready at the border

The e-Visa portal lists travel documents, evidence of purpose, accommodation, insurance and sufficient funds among its border-document requirements. Treat supporting evidence as part of preparation, rather than assuming a passport or approved visa answers every possible question.

Organise the folder around your actual trip: accommodation addresses for the nights booked, a clear route, transport arrangements and an explanation of how you will pay. If staying with someone, keep their address and contact details accessible. Do not present bookings or statements that misrepresent your plans.
A short, realistic itinerary is easier to explain than a long list of places you cannot visit in the available time. Our
guide to how many days you need in Georgia
can help you choose a sensible route before finalising accommodation.
Common mistakes to avoid

The biggest mistake is mixing rules from different entry routes. A passport-based exemption, a foreign-residence exemption and a Georgian e-Visa have different conditions. Check the one you will actually use.

Another is checking only the lead traveller's documents. Make a simple list for every person and confirm that the policy dates match the trip, including the departure day. Repeat the check if flights change.
Finally, separate admission planning from arrival logistics. Once your entry documents are settled, organise your first night's accommodation and transfer. Our
Tbilisi airport transport guide
explains the practical next step after arrival.

faq.question: Do I need a visa to visit Georgia in 2026?
faq.answer: It depends on your citizenship, passport type and any qualifying foreign visa or residence permit. Many listed nationalities have visa-free entry, while other travellers need an e-Visa or consular visa. Check your circumstances through the official Georgian consular portal before booking.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Georgia?
faq.answer: Yes, incoming tourists covered by Decree No. 602 need health and accident insurance with at least 30,000 GEL of cover for the full stay, including arrival and departure dates. The policy must be available in Georgian or English, on paper or electronically; specified exemptions apply.

faq.question: Do all GCC residents need one year left on their residence permit?
faq.answer: No. The stricter one-year-remaining-validity condition concerns 17 specified nationalities using the relevant Gulf visa or residence-permit route. GCC citizens and other foreign residents must check their own entry category. Read the linked official guidance rather than applying this condition to everyone.

faq.question: Can Indian passport holders enter Georgia without a visa?
faq.answer: A qualifying foreign visa or residence permit may allow visa-free entry under the relevant conditions. An ordinary Indian passport alone does not establish general one-year visa-free eligibility. Otherwise, check the official e-Visa or consular application route for your documents.

faq.question: Can I buy travel insurance when I arrive in Georgia?
faq.answer: Arrange compliant cover before departure. Do not rely on a policy being sold at the border. Check that the insurance starts in time for arrival and lasts through departure, and keep the policy available offline.

set.title: Kassland Georgia: Diamond Bridge Tickets, Hours & Tips
set.metaTitle: Kassland Georgia: Diamond Bridge Tickets, Hours & Tips
set.metaDescription: Visit Kassland Georgia with verified Diamond Bridge ticket prices, opening hours and transport tips from Tbilisi. Plan a canyon day and avoid booking mix-ups.
set.excerpt: Plan a Kassland day trip from Tbilisi with current canyon ticket prices, Diamond Bridge opening hours, transport options and advice for families.

children.text: Kassland Georgia is the home of the Diamond Bridge, a 240-metre glass walkway above Tsalka Canyon, also called Dashbashi Canyon. For a visit from Tbilisi, the useful questions are what the ticket costs, which activities it covers and how much of the day to allow. This guide puts those decisions first, with official booking links and a practical plan for the canyon.
Prices and operating information checked on 27 October 2026. Recheck your chosen ticket and the weather before travelling.
Kassland tickets and opening hours: the quick answer
The
canyon ticket page linked by Kass Land
currently lists these categories:
Standard canyon ticket: 79 GEL.
Georgian citizen ticket: 46 GEL; check the identification required for this category.
Swing: 35 GEL.
Bikeline: 120 GEL.
The operator links to a separate
Kass Land Attraction Park booking page
. That page lists an unlimited attractions and giant-trampolines package at 59 GEL, a resident version at 35 GEL and an eight-minute adult go-kart session at 44 GEL.

These are different products. Check the inclusions for the exact ticket you select, especially bridge access, the canyon trail and any extra activity. Do not assume an attraction-park package includes the canyon, or that the standard canyon ticket includes every ride. Child eligibility and discounts need checking separately.
The operator's
Plan Your Visit page

lists the canyon and Glass Bridge & Diamond 360 as open daily, 10:00–19:00. It lists the bike line Monday–Saturday, 10:00–18:30. Treat those as the advertised hours, not a promise that every attraction will operate throughout your visit: ask about last admission, trail access and weather restrictions.
Where is the Diamond Bridge in Georgia?

The Diamond Bridge is at Kass Land in the Tsalka area, near Dashbashi village in the country of Georgia. It is not a bridge in central Tbilisi. Searches for Kassland, Kass Land, Tsalka Canyon and Dashbashi Canyon often refer to different parts of the same destination.
The
operator's booking hub

describes the drive as around 90 minutes from Tbilisi. For planning, allow roughly 1.5–2 hours each way, with extra time for city traffic, breaks or poor weather. Your departure address and the day's road conditions matter more than a single advertised journey time.

Save the venue's entrance location before leaving. A map pin for Tsalka town or a general canyon viewpoint may not take you to the correct visitor entrance. If using a driver, agree on the entrance and pickup point rather than asking only for “the canyon.”
Is Kassland worth visiting?

Kassland makes most sense when you specifically want the glass bridge, canyon scenery or paid adventure activities. It can provide a different kind of day between city sightseeing and winery visits. Choose it because those experiences appeal to your group, rather than assuming every Georgia itinerary needs the same stop.

It is a weaker fit if you dislike heights, have only a short stay in Tbilisi or want an inexpensive nature walk. The bridge is a major part of the appeal, and travel plus admission takes a meaningful share of the day and budget. Decide whether you would still enjoy the trip if a particular ride were unavailable.

For a family, ask each person what they actually want to do. One traveller may want the sky bike, another the canyon walk, and someone else may prefer a relaxed lunch. That conversation is more useful than buying every possible activity in advance.
Compare the destination with our
best day trips from Tbilisi
. A history-focused day and an adventure-park visit satisfy different interests; choose the one your group is most likely to enjoy.
How much should you budget for the day?

Start with transport, then add the exact ticket categories, optional activities and meals. Keeping these separate helps when comparing an independent visit with a tour quotation. A low transport price can look attractive until you discover that admission and waiting time are additional.

For two adults using the listed standard canyon category, the tickets alone total 158 GEL. If one adult adds the listed swing, that becomes 193 GEL before transport and food. This is an illustrative calculation from the prices above, not a bundled offer.

Do not multiply the adult price by the size of a family without checking children's categories first. Equally, do not assume a child can join a ride because there is a family ticket elsewhere in the park. Ask about the current height, age, weight and supervision rules for each activity.
When requesting transport, ask for a written total that makes clear whether it includes the return journey, waiting time, parking and any other stops. Our
Georgia trip budget guide
can help you decide how much to allocate to this day within the whole holiday.
Getting to Kassland from Tbilisi
Private driver

A private driver can make the day easier when travelling with children, combining different activities or wanting a flexible return time. Agree on how long the driver will wait and what happens if your visit runs late. Specify any child-seat needs before confirming.

For a first visit, a simple out-and-back plan is easier to manage than several widely separated stops. Tell the driver whether you intend to walk the canyon trail, since that affects the time you need on site. Our
private-driver guide
explains what to ask when comparing arrangements.
Rental car

Driving yourself gives you control over breaks and departure time. Before setting out, check the weather and route, save offline directions and allow time to find the correct entrance and parking. Choose a return time that leaves a comfortable margin, especially when daylight is limited.

Avoid treating the advertised journey time as a deadline. If the weather deteriorates, revise the plan rather than trying to recover time on unfamiliar roads. A day trip should leave room for a slower journey home.
Shared excursion or public transport

For a shared excursion, confirm the time at Kassland, ticket inclusions and cancellation arrangements. A description that says “Diamond Bridge tour” may refer to transport and a stop at the venue; inspect the inclusions before comparing its total with a self-planned visit.

If investigating public transport, verify both the outward service and the final connection to the visitor entrance, plus the return. Do not build the day around an unverified direct bus or assume a late return taxi will be available. This guide does not list a current confirmed public-transport timetable.
The bridge, canyon walk and extra attractions

Think of the visit as several choices rather than one continuous activity. The glass bridge is the signature viewpoint. The operator also advertises a nature trail, waterfalls, a sky bike, a swing and a separate attractions park.

Walking in the canyon is a different undertaking from crossing the bridge. Ask staff about the route, surface, steps, current access and the return climb before starting. Wear shoes with grip and carry water. Do not assume a canyon trail is step-free or suitable for a pushchair because the wider venue welcomes families.

If heights worry you, discuss the layout with staff before buying tickets. A ground-based activity may suit you better, but confirm how it is reached and whether the route itself involves exposure. There is no need for everyone in a group to choose the same optional ride.
A realistic day-trip plan
Here is a suggested sequence, not an operator timetable:
Leave Tbilisi in the morning, allowing for the journey and the venue's advertised opening time.
At arrival, confirm weather conditions, ticket inclusions and which activities are running.
Visit the bridge while keeping time for photographs and pauses.
Choose the canyon walk or a paid activity according to energy, comfort and conditions.
Take a meal break and allow a flexible return journey.

As a planning allowance, reserve about 2–4 hours on site, depending on walking pace, queues, meals and activities. With travel, that usually means setting aside most of the day. A quick bridge-only stop is different from a family visit with walking and rides.

For an autumn or winter trip, check daylight as well as the advertised closing time. A venue remaining open into the evening does not mean you will have the same light for canyon views or the same conditions for walking.
Visiting with children: what to check first

Before paying, confirm children's ticket categories, supervision requirements and restrictions for each ride. Bring layers and footwear appropriate for an outdoor day. Choose one priority activity, then treat anything else as optional.

For pushchairs, mobility limitations or a family member who tires easily, ask the venue which areas are accessible from the entrance and where rest stops are available. Keep the walking plan realistic for the least mobile person in your group.
Our
Tbilisi with kids guide
offers alternatives if an all-day excursion feels too ambitious. A shorter city activity may fit better after a late arrival or before an early flight.
Before you book

Check the canyon and attraction-park products separately, confirm the return transport and ask about the activities you care about most. Keep the booking confirmation accessible offline. If a weather-dependent ride is the reason for your visit, check its operating status before leaving Tbilisi.
Once you have those answers, Kassland becomes easier to place in an itinerary: one deliberately planned outdoor day, with a clear budget and enough time to enjoy it.

faq.question: How much are Kassland Diamond Bridge tickets?
faq.answer: The operator-linked canyon booking page listed a standard ticket at 79 GEL and a Georgian citizen ticket at 46 GEL when checked on 27 October 2026. The swing and bikeline were separate options at 35 GEL and 120 GEL. Confirm the selected ticket's bridge and trail inclusions before paying.

faq.question: What are the Diamond Bridge opening hours?
faq.answer: Kass Land advertises the canyon and Glass Bridge & Diamond 360 as open daily from 10:00 to 19:00. Recheck last admission, trail access and weather-related restrictions before travelling.

faq.question: Where is the Diamond Bridge, and how far is it from Tbilisi?
faq.answer: It is at Kass Land near Dashbashi village in the Tsalka area of Georgia. The operator advertises approximately 90 minutes from Tbilisi; allow around 1.5–2 hours each way as a planning estimate, depending on traffic, weather and your starting point.

faq.question: Does a Kassland ticket include every attraction?
faq.answer: Do not assume so. The operator links to separate canyon and attraction-park products, with additional activities listed separately. Read the inclusions for the exact ticket or package you choose.

faq.question: Is Kassland suitable for children or visitors afraid of heights?
faq.answer: It depends on the person and chosen activity. Check children's eligibility and ride restrictions with staff, and ask about access to the canyon trail. The glass bridge involves height exposure, and an outdoor trail should not be assumed to be step-free or pushchair-friendly.
